content:
marta: Quick one — proposing a new "usage-smoothing credits" add-on to reduce immediate overage churn for customers with spiky traffic. Idea: customers buy a monthly buffer of tokens that auto-consume on short spikes, smoothing billing and avoiding emergency contract negotiations. Thoughts?

thomas: +1 conceptually. question: does this apply to both generation and embeddings? also: how does it interact with Dedicated reserved capacity?

samir: we should flag revenue recognition and legal. If credits are prepaid and expire monthly we can treat as deferred revenue; but refunds/rollovers complicate SOC2 + accounting. pinging accounting to validate.

jen: can we outline launch guardrails before we iterate? what do we need to consider for SLAs and abuse prevention? e.g., can a customer use smoothing to mask sustained overuse that should trigger a capacity upgrade?

marta: good calls. answers: 1) covers text generation + embeddings by default (separate SKUs). 2) for Dedicated customers smoothing credits are a billing layer only — they cannot bypass reserved capacity limits (we'd bill for over-reserved usage and apply smoothing credits to the invoice). 3) credits expire monthly and do not roll over.

thomas: ok on dedicated. for Hosted customers, does smoothing auto-top-up or do we require explicit add-on purchase? want to avoid surprise charges.

marta: plan is opt-in add-on only. we will offer an automatic top-up toggle (customers can opt into a small auto-top-up threshold with notifications). defaults: OFF.

samir: accounting-bot: quick verify — deferred revenue ok if non-refundable, monthly expiry. also need language for contracts re: refunds and credits on termination.

accounting-bot: Confirmed: prepaid, non-refundable credits with monthly expiry are standard. Need contract clause for termination and for enterprise negotiated exceptions.

jen: launch criteria suggestion: 
- Pilot with 3 customers (mix of SMB, PMF start-up, 1 enterprise) for 2 billing cycles
- No more than 3% revenue leakage vs baseline (measure by simulated top-ups)
- Abuse detection in place (rate-limit + manual review for >30% sustained usage vs rolling 30d)
- UI/console: SKU shown on billing page + clear consumption view + opt-in modal with examples

marta: pricing mock for discussion (rough):
```
Smoothing credits (hosted):
- SMC-100K : 100k tokens/mo - $120/mo
- SMC-1M   : 1M tokens/mo   - $900/mo
- SMC-10M  : 10M tokens/mo  - $7,500/mo
Dedicated: buffer purchasable but billed as invoice credit, no autoscale pass-through.
```

thomas: pricing looks ok as a starting point. we should model elasticity — i.e., how often customers actually hit buffer. Recommend a 12% margin target vs on-demand to protect unit economics.

samir: add-on contract constraints: 
- Not combinable with committed overage forgiveness deals unless explicitly negotiated.
- For enterprise deals we must surface smoothing as a negotiable clause (can allow rollovers / refunds in specific SOW).

jen: ops question — any infra work required? e.g., meter pipeline changes to tag smoothing consumption so we don't double count caching/batching savings?

marta: minimal infra: tag smoothing-consumed tokens at billing pipeline, and add an alert if smoothing consumption > 50% of total tokens in a billing window (pilot threshold). We'll file an eng ticket.

thomas: can we do experiment variants: A — fixed buffer SKU; B — usage-based smoothing priced as % of overage (e.g., 25% discount on first X overage tokens). That could help for customers who don't want monthly commitment.

marta: good idea. include in pilot. ops: will notify sales+support to add recommended messaging.

jen: final ask — let's get a short one-pager for sales: what it solves, examples, pricing options, and launch checklist. I'll own the one-pager.

marta: thanks all. next steps: 1) jen to draft one-pager by EOW; 2) accounting to confirm contract language (samir); 3) eng ticket for meter tagging (marta to file); 4) select 3 pilot customers (sales + AE team). tagging @sales for pilot candidate suggestions. :thumbsup:
